caveat: Run against a local SeaweedFS S3 server. Behaviour of Railway Buckets and Cloudflare R2 must be re-measured with this same script on the approved staging buckets.

rows.name: browser XHR PUT with the exact signed headers succeeds cross-origin
Blob type alone (no explicit header) is sent as the signed Content-Type
a Blob with NO type and no header is refused (the browser sends no usable Content-Type)
a different Content-Type than the one signed is refused
a body one byte larger or smaller than the signed length is refused
an extra x-amz-acl: public-read header is blocked by the CORS allow-list, and the object is never public
rows.expected: browser blocks (status 0), nothing stored, anonymous GET 403/404

rows.name: modified key, extended expiry and a stripped signature are refused
cancelling (xhr.abort) a slow upload fires onabort and stores nothing
the same signed URL can be retried after a cancel (within its lifetime) and completes
one dropped connection mid-upload: Chromium retries the PUT itself (the page may see success after two wire attempts)
rows.expected: either success after a transparent retry or a network error; never a partial object

rows.name: repeated dropped connections surface as a network error (status 0) and store nothing
retrying the same URL after repeated drops succeeds
offline fails fast as a network error; back online the retry succeeds and re-writing the same key is idempotent
rows.expected: offline status 0; then 200; one object of the right size

rows.name: a re-issued signed URL for the same key (the re-init path) overwrites it with identical bytes
no anonymous read, list or write; a signature cannot be reused for another method or another workspace prefix
signed GET: forced headers, readable cross-origin, usable in , no Referer sent
rows.expected: type image/jpeg, inline, no-store; image loads; no referer

observed.note: Content-Disposition is not CORS-safelisted, so script cannot read it unless the bucket exposes it; does not need it

rows.name: a page on a non-allow-listed origin is blocked by CORS and nothing is stored
